sources.title: Can I go to Australia?
sources.officialityEvidence: The Department of Home Affairs publishes this entry guidance on its immi.homeaffairs.gov.au domain.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Australian passport holders do not need a visa to enter Australia.

sources.title: New Zealand citizens
sources.officialityEvidence: The Department of Home Affairs publishes this New Zealand entry guidance on its immi.homeaffairs.gov.au domain.
sources.supportingExcerpt: New Zealand citizens with a valid New Zealand passport do not need to apply for a visa before coming to Australia.

sources.title: Subclass 601 Electronic Travel Authority
sources.officialityEvidence: The Department of Home Affairs publishes the ETA subclass eligibility and application guidance on its immi.homeaffairs.gov.au domain.
sources.supportingExcerpt: You must hold a valid passport from one of these countries or jurisdictions to be eligible for an ETA.

sources.title: Subclass 651 eVisitor
sources.officialityEvidence: The Department of Home Affairs publishes the eVisitor subclass eligibility and application guidance on its immi.homeaffairs.gov.au domain.
sources.supportingExcerpt: You must be a citizen of and hold a valid passport from one of these countries to be eligible for the eVisitor.

sources.title: Visitor visa (subclass 600): Tourist stream (apply outside Australia)
sources.officialityEvidence: The Department of Home Affairs publishes this Visitor visa subclass guidance on its immi.homeaffairs.gov.au domain.
sources.supportingExcerpt: This visa stream lets you visit Australia as a tourist, to go on a cruise or to visit family and friends.

policies.title: Australian citizens: automatic right of entry
policies.summary: Australian passport holders do not need a visa to enter Australia.
conditions: This is citizenship access; it does not describe entry rights for non-citizen Australian travel documents.
An Australian citizen holding another ETA-eligible passport cannot apply for an ETA.

policies.title: New Zealand citizens: Special Category visa on arrival
policies.summary: New Zealand citizens with a valid New Zealand passport do not apply before travel and can apply for a Special Category visa (subclass 444) on entry.
conditions: Requires New Zealand citizenship and a valid New Zealand passport.
The SCV is granted only if its criteria are met; Home Affairs identifies character requirements as material.
This policy is distinct from ETA and eVisitor eligibility and does not extend to non-New Zealand family members.

application.label: Home Affairs New Zealand citizen entry guidance
steps: Travel with a valid New Zealand passport.
On entry, apply for the Special Category visa (subclass 444).
Meet the SCV criteria at entry.

policies.title: Electronic Travel Authority (subclass 601) eligible ordinary passports
policies.summary: Holders of the listed eligible passports may apply outside Australia for an ETA for temporary visitor travel, subject to the stated nationality and document conditions.
conditions: The ETA page lists eligible countries or jurisdictions and requires a valid passport.
This policy excludes non-citizen passports, certificates of identity, and other travel documents such as a Titre de Voyage.
TW: excludes official and diplomatic passports.
GB: applies to British Citizen and British National (Overseas) passport statuses; the ISO code does not distinguish those British document statuses.
AU citizens cannot use this route, even if they also hold an ETA-eligible passport.
Applicants must be outside Australia when they apply and when the ETA is granted; each traveller applies separately.
For visitor purposes, Home Affairs describes stays of up to 3 months each entry during a 12-month validity period.
A criminal conviction may require a Visitor visa (subclass 600) instead; grant and border entry remain conditional.

application.label: Australian ETA app guidance
steps: Confirm the eligible passport and any document-status condition.
Outside Australia, use the Australian ETA app with the passport to be used for travel.
Scan the passport, provide a live image and required information, pay the service fee, and submit.
Travel only after an ETA is granted and use the passport linked to it.

policies.title: eVisitor (subclass 651) eligible ordinary passports
policies.summary: Citizens holding a valid passport from the listed countries may apply outside Australia online for a free eVisitor for temporary visitor travel.
conditions: Applicants must be citizens of, and hold a valid passport from, a listed country.
This policy excludes non-citizen passports, certificates of identity, Titre de Voyage documents, and the listed non-British-Citizen British passport statuses.
GB: applies only to British Citizen passports.
VA: the passport must indicate nationality of Vatican City (Holy See).
Applicants must be outside Australia when applying and when the visa is decided; each traveller applies separately.
For visitor purposes, the eVisitor is valid for travel for 12 months and permits stays up to 3 months each entry.
A criminal conviction or prior health-requirement failure directs the applicant to consider Visitor visa (subclass 600) instead; grant and border entry remain conditional.
Twenty-four listed ISO codes also have an ETA option; the concurrent ETA route is retained separately rather than reclassified.

application.label: Home Affairs eVisitor online application guidance
steps: Confirm citizenship, valid passport, and any British or Vatican document-status condition.
Outside Australia, create the eVisitor application online.
Travel only after written grant of the visa.
